newsitem.title: MAURITANIA: Mauritania launches legislative election campaign.
newsitem.headline: Mauritania launches legislative election campaign.

text.p: Mauritania opened campaigning for its October 11 parliamentary election on Wednesday, with women standing for the first time and the main opposition opting against a repeat of their boycott of the 1992 poll.

But analysts say the ruling Democratic and Social Republican Party (PRDS) is likely to have the edge in the race for the 79 seats in the new assembly because opposition parties are ill-prepared and have failed to forge a united front.
Mauritania straddles black and Arab Africa.
The elections are the first test of the multi-party politicial system introduced by President Maaouya Ould Sid'Ahmed Taya in 1991 and launched with presidential and parliamentary elections in 1992.
Taya, who seized power in a bloodless coup in 1984, won a six-year term in the presidential poll. The National Assembly has a five-year mandate.
Thirteen political parties will contest the October 11 election plus 52 independents, many of them members of the ruling party passed over during the selection of candidates for the poll.
Most of the 26 women candidates are from the ruling party.
